content:
sam: heads-up — we're seeing a sustained p99 spike on hosted /v1/generate starting ~11:14 UTC, p95 up too. queue depth jumped from ~8 to ~60 on a handful of shards.

mira: looking at graphs now, KV cache hit rate dropped ~40% on the affected shards, priming churn visible. any recent model rollouts?

kevin: no rollout from product. the kernel-selector logs show a wave of kernel swaps to `aux` kernel at the same time — likely fallback due to batch shape mismatch.

sara: noisy tenant? igrep on tenant tags shows a tenant with lots of short requests (avg tokens 12) spiking rps to a few GPUs. priming thrash + small seqs = bad batch packing.

infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-api-p99 > 1.2s for /v1/generate (shard-group-7). threshold=1.0s

sam: can someone dump recent scheduler decisions and kernel-selector trace for shard-group-7?

kevin: grabbing traces, sending small extract:```json
{
  "ts": 1733334438,
  "shard": "sg-7",
  "kernel_decision": "aux_fallback",
  "reason": "batch_shape_mismatch",
  "queue_depth": 48
}
```

mira: profiling snippet from host: `nvprof` shows more kernel launches but much shorter runtimes — overhead dominates. KV cache eviction rate spiked 3x. suspect KV priming is forcing many short KV builds.

sara: workaround idea: throttle that noisy tenant at the rate limiter to smooth batch packing, and temporarily pin kernel-selector to prefer primary kernel when possible. risk: we'll hit some slow kernels for genuinely mismatched sequences.

eng-runtime-oncall: agree with mitigations. I'm applying a soft ratecap (burst=200, rate=120rps) for tenant X on the hosted tier and adding a kernel-selector override for shard-group-7 to bias primary kernel for 10m.

sam: applied — seeing queue depth start to come down from 60 -> 20 in last 90s. p95 trending down. :thumbsup:

kevin: follow-up data: after override, aux_fallback events dropped 85%, KV eviction rate reduced, but average batch size increased only slightly (1.6 -> 2.3). still room to improve packing heuristics.

mira: captured a flame for the worst window — primary kernel shows stable per-token time but overhead fixed cost is smaller. we should tune sampler hysteresis to prefer waiting for a small extra 10–30ms for better packing on short-seq traffic.

sara: opened an RFC issue for batching-sampler hysteresis + tenant-weighted throttles (link: https://rwd.internal/eng/runtime/issue/4321).

eng-runtime-oncall: will keep the soft caps for 30m and monitor. if p99 stays < 800ms we can revert override and roll a sampler tweak in a canary.

sam: note for postmortem: root cause = noisy short-request tenant causing KV priming churn + kernel-selector fallback due to transient batch-shape distribution shift. mitigation = soft tenant ratecap + kernel bias + next-step = sampler hysteresis tuning + maybe KV prefetch heuristics for short seqs.

kevin: also adding a small profiling job (5m window) to detect priming storms early and auto-suggest tenant caps. i'll add metrics to the console dashboard.

mira: thanks — leaving traces and logs in the incident folder: `/var/log/rl-infra/sg7/1733334444/` and adding a couple of example rpc traces in the ticket.

sam: good rescue work. keep an eye; i'll ping again if anything reappears.

infra-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: hosted-api-p99 returned to baseline (0.62s) — resolved by eng-runtime-oncall actions.
